headline: San Juan Mountain Wilderness and Historic District Entry
reservation: Telluride Town Park camping and high-end glamping sites require reservations 6–12 months in advance. The gondola is free and requires no ticket, but peak festival weekends cause significant wait times at all transit points.

days.title: Box Canyon Floor and Vertical Transit

stops.name: San Miguel River Trail
stops.detail: Walk the flat, scenic path along the valley floor to acclimate to 8,750 feet.

stops.name: Free Telluride Gondola
stops.detail: Ride to San Sophia Station for 360-degree views of the San Juan Mountains.

days.driving: Walking town; no vehicle needed for most central activities.
days.note: Stay hydrated; the high altitude and dry air can cause rapid dehydration.

days.title: Waterfalls and Alpine Basins

stops.name: Bridal Veil Falls
stops.detail: View the tallest free-falling waterfall in Colorado at 365 feet.

stops.name: Bear Creek Falls Trail
stops.detail: Hike through aspen groves to a powerful cascade visible from the town end.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes to reach Bridal Veil parking; road is rugged.
days.note: The road to the top of Bridal Veil is narrow and requires high-clearance 4WD.

days.title: High Mountain Passes and Lakes

stops.name: Trout Lake
stops.detail: Drive south to this high-alpine lake for kayaking or lakeside photography.

stops.name: Mountain Village Center
stops.detail: Explore the modern mountain hub for shopping and outdoor gear orientation.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes round trip to Trout Lake; paved but winding.
days.note: Check weather for mountain passes; snow can occur in any month at these heights.

intel.title: Town Perimeter Parking
intel.text: Parking in the historic core is strictly metered and limited; use the Carbondale lot or Mountain Village parking for longer stays. Town Park fills early for all trail access.

intel.title: Canyon Signal Strength
intel.text: Reliable 4G is available in the town and Mountain Village, but signal drops immediately upon entering Bear Creek or Bridal Veil basins. Satellite messengers are suggested for backcountry.

intel.title: San Miguel Valley Fuel
intel.text: Refuel in Telluride or Placerville before heading south toward Lizard Head Pass. There are no service stations on the high mountain passes toward Ouray.

intel.title: Gondola Service Windows
intel.text: The gondola usually closes for maintenance in the shoulder seasons (May and November); verify these dates before planning a visit. Daily service typically runs late into the evening.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: High-altitude routes like Black Bear Pass and Imogene Pass are only open a few weeks in late summer. Check San Miguel County road reports for specific opening dates.

plan.arrival: Pickup at Montrose Regional (MTJ) for a 90-minute drive or TEX for 15 minutes; check-in and use the free gondola for initial orientation.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for town, but 4WD is essential for Black Bear Pass or high-altitude trailheads; check rental insurance for off-road use.
plan.goldenHour: San Sophia Station at the gondola mid-point for the alpenglow effect on the Wilson Range.
